title: Slow Is How You Fly
summary: A nervous little dragon learns that with calm, anything is possible.

scenes.text: High on top of a green mountain, where the clouds passed so close you could touch them with your paw, lived a little dragon named Tito. Tito was small, no bigger than a medium puppy, and his scales shone like pieces of fire when the morning sun hit them. He had two short wings with golden edges and a curled-up tail that ended in a point. But Tito had a very big problem for someone so small: every time he was about to fly, he forgot how. His wings would freeze, standing still at his sides, not knowing what to do. And then something would start pounding hard inside his chest: his heart. Meanwhile, his dragon friends flew happily among the clouds, doing pirouettes in the air, chasing each other with laughter and puffing out breaths of sparks. Tito watched them from his corner on the mountain, his belly pressed to the ground. "I want to fly too," he thought quietly, biting his tail. But the moment he opened his wings, everything left his head, as if someone stole the trick from him.

One clear morning, Tito decided that today was the day. He climbed onto a big rock with firm steps, puffed up his chest like he had seen his dad do, closed his eyes tight, and got ready. "Come on, Tito, you can do it," he told himself. He counted three, two, one, and jumped. For just a second he felt the wind on his face and thought "I did it!" But then his wings tangled up, one crossed over the other, and... Splat! He fell flat on the ground, his nose full of leaves and a yellow flower stuck to his forehead. A butterfly flying nearby laughed so hard she got dizzy and landed sideways on a branch. Tito got very sad. A lump formed in his throat and two big tears wet his scales. "Never, never, never am I going to be able to fly," sighed the little dragon, and lay down belly-up, looking at the sky.

The butterfly, now recovered from her laughter, felt sorry for the little dragon. She flew down slowly and landed on his nose. She had orange wings with black dots, like a flower with spots. "Forgive me, I wasn't laughing at you," she whispered. "It's just that you get so stiff. You think too much." Tito opened one eye, then the other. The butterfly continued: "I'm going to tell you a secret, okay? Close your eyes. Now breathe. Deeply, like this, watch how I do it." The butterfly puffed up her belly and let the air out with a soft blow. Tito copied her. "Again. One more time. Imagine the clouds, imagine the wind on your wings. Don't think about flying. Your wings already know. We just have to leave them alone." Tito did everything the butterfly told him. He took in air once, twice, three times, four. His heart, which before jumped like a rabbit, began to beat slowly. His belly grew warm.

When Tito opened his eyes, something magical was happening: his wings were already moving on their own. They went up and down with a soft rhythm, without him thinking about it, as if they were doing what they had always known how to do. Suddenly, Tito noticed that his feet stopped touching the ground. He looked down. The rock was far away. The flowers got smaller and smaller. He was flying! He rose high, high, until he brushed the white clouds with the tip of his tail. He felt the cool wind on his face, on his ears, on every scale. And he let out a laugh. With it came a puff of golden sparkles that drew a heart in the air. From far away, his dragon friends clapped for him with their wings. The butterfly danced beside him, happy. That afternoon, Tito learned a secret he would remember all his life: every time fear got the best of him, he would breathe deeply like his friend taught him, and everything would become easier.
